raw_extract: Cotisations salariales - Salarie du secteur prive. Verifie le 01 janvier 2026 - Service Public / Direction de l'information legale et administrative (Premier ministre). En plus des cotisations sociales versees par l'employeur, les cotisations salariales sont deduites du salaire brut du salarie. Le taux et l'assiette qui sont appliques varient en fonction des cotisations concernees. Cotisations de securite sociale. Tableau - Taux et assiette des cotisations sociales. Type de cotisation | Assiette de cotisation | Taux. Assurance vieillesse deplafonnee (retraite du regime general) | Montant du salaire | 0,40 %. Assurance vieillesse plafonnee (retraite du regime general) | Montant du salaire jusqu'a 4 005 EUR par mois | 6,90 %. Contributions sociales (CSG/CRDS). Contribution sociale generalisee (CSG) | 98,25 % du salaire brut, dans la limite de 192 240 EUR ; 100 % au-dela de ce montant | 9,2 %, dont 2,4 % non deductibles du revenu imposable. Contribution au remboursement de la dette sociale (CRDS) | 98,25 % du salaire brut, dans la limite de 192 240 EUR ; 100 % au-dela de ce montant | 0,5 % non deductible du revenu imposable. Cotisations de chomage: La cotisation salariale d'assurance chomage a ete supprimee totalement depuis le 1er octobre 2018. Cotisations de retraite complementaire. Agirc-Arrco | Tranche 1 : jusqu'a 4 005 EUR par mois | 3,15 %. | Tranche 2 : entre 4 005 EUR et 32 040 EUR par mois | 8,64 %. Contribution d'equilibre general (CEG) | Tranche 1 : jusqu'a 4 005 EUR par mois | 0,86 %. | Tranche 2 : entre 4 005 EUR et 32 040 EUR par mois | 1,08 %. Contribution d'equilibre technique (CET) | Tranche 1 : jusqu'a 4 005 EUR par mois | Pas de cotisation. | Tranche 1 et Tranche 2 : entre 4 005 EUR et 32 040 EUR par mois | 0,14 %. A savoir: La remuneration d'un salarie de 65 ans ou plus est soumise a une contribution specifique solidarite. Elle s'eleve a 2,4 % du salaire brut.

claims.unit: EUR per month (net a payer / take-home, after prelevement a la source)
claims.statement: Derived 'net a payer' (take-home) of EUR 2,205.69 per month from a gross monthly salary of EUR 2,800.53, using only rates and ceilings published by Service Public. Employee social contributions deducted from gross: EUR 572.44 per month = 20.4403 per cent of gross, comprising base retirement (capped) 6.90 per cent on the salary up to EUR 4,005 per month = EUR 193.24; base retirement (uncapped) 0.40 per cent, nil here because the salary is below the EUR 4,005 ceiling; CSG 9.2 per cent plus CRDS 0.5 per cent applied to 98.25 per cent of gross = EUR 266.90; Agirc-Arrco tranche 1 3.15 per cent up to EUR 4,005 = EUR 88.22; CEG tranche 1 0.86 per cent up to EUR 4,005 = EUR 24.08; CET nil below the ceiling; APEC nil (cadres only). No employee unemployment-insurance contribution applies, per the source. 'Net a payer avant impot sur le revenu' is therefore EUR 2,228.09 per month.

claims.unit: EUR per month (net apres cotisations sociales, i.e. 'net a payer AVANT prelevement a la source')
claims.statement: The French gross-to-net figure before income tax: EUR 2,800.53 gross minus EUR 572.44 of employee social contributions = EUR 2,228.09 per month. This is the figure a French payslip labels 'Net a payer avant impot sur le revenu' and it is the amount most French sources mean when they say 'salaire net'. It is NOT the same as Anglo-Saxon take-home, because income tax is withheld from it separately.

claims.unit: EUR per month (revenu net imposable mensuel, the withholding base)
claims.statement: The monthly 'net imposable' on which prelevement a la source is calculated at the same gross of EUR 2,800.53: EUR 2,228.09 after social contributions, less EUR 187.12 of deductible CSG (6.8 per cent applied to 98.25 per cent of gross), less the 10 per cent allowance with its EUR 142 monthly floor (EUR 204.11), less the professional deduction of 0.34 x the annual social security ceiling divided by twelve (EUR 113.48) = EUR 1,723.42 per month.

assumptions: salary of EUR 2,800.53 gross per month is a STATED INPUT, taken from the corpus's existing official French figure (the carte de sejour recherche d'emploi/creation d'entreprise salary floor, service-public.fr). It is not a claim about what a French graduate typically earns
private-sector employee ('Salarie du secteur prive'), under 65, and NOT classed as cadre, so the APEC contribution (0.024 per cent) is excluded; a cadre would pay slightly less take-home
the 2026 social security ceiling used by Service Public on this page, EUR 4,005 per month (tranche 1 to EUR 4,005; tranche 2 to EUR 32,040), and the CSG/CRDS ceiling of EUR 192,240
monthly-paid, twelve equal months, no variable pay, no employer-paid benefits in kind
the 10 per cent net-imposable allowance is applied rather than its EUR 142 monthly floor, because at this salary the 10 per cent amount (EUR 204.11) exceeds the floor
the 0.34 x annual-plafond professional deduction is divided by twelve to a monthly basis

THE WITHHOLDING RATE APPLIED IN CLAIM 001 IS MINE, NOT THE SOURCE'S. The prelevement a la source rate of 1.3 per cent was obtained by looking up the EUR 1,723.42 net imposable in the official DGFiP default-rate grid archived in FR/021_net_monthly_income_pas_grille_officielle.json. That grid is a DEFAULT grid applied when the administration cannot determine a taxpayer's personal rate; a real employee's rate is individually determined and is reconciled with the final income tax bill at year end, with any over-withholding refunded by the following summer.
notes: READ THIS BEFORE USING THE NUMBER, BECAUSE FRANCE HAS THREE DIFFERENT THINGS CALLED 'NET' AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS TAKE-HOME PAY. The French Ministry of Solidarity defines them on its own payslip guidance (see the companion artifact 021): 'le "net a payer", qui figure le plus souvent en bas du bulletin de paie, correspond au montant effectivement verse au salarie' and it 'tient compte de toutes les deductions, notamment de l'ensemble des cotisations sociales et du prelevement a la source' - that is the true take-home and is claim fr-net-monthly-001. The same document warns that this figure 'prend egalement en compte certains elements annexes (ex : saisies sur salaires, remboursement de frais professionnels, participation du salarie aux titres restaurants, retenue pour la cantine, etc.)'. The same document separately distinguishes 'net a payer avant impot sur le revenu' - gross minus social contributions only, claim fr-net-monthly-002 - which is the figure most French media and most French job advertisements mean by 'salaire net', and 'net fiscal (ou net imposable)' - the PAS base, claim fr-net-monthly-003 - which is neither of the others. THAT IS THE SINGLE BIGGEST MISREADING RISK IN THIS ENTIRE CORPUS: a French 'net' salary quoted as a break-even income is normally EUR 2,228.09, not EUR 2,205.69, and is NOT comparable to a German Netentgelt or a British take-home. A THIRD, LARGER MISREADING RISK, and the reason the corpus should probably prefer claim 002 over claim 001: the prelevement a la source is ADVANCE WITHHOLDING, not a final liability. A person earning EUR 2,800.53 gross with no other income and no deductions would in practice have a final annual income tax liability of zero or near zero, so the EUR 22.40 withheld would be refunded in full and their actual annual take-home would be EUR 2,228.09 per month, not EUR 2,205.69. Claim 001 is therefore a conservative monthly cash-flow figure for a paycheque read in isolation, not an annual outcome. EVERY RATE IN CLAIM 001 COMES FROM THIS ONE OFFICIAL PAGE - I did not apply a guessed aggregate percentage - but two deduction steps were applied from general French tax rules rather than from this page: the 10 per cent net-imposable allowance and the 0.34 plafond professional deduction. Both are standard, non-optional statutory deductions and both are flagged in the assumptions list as mine. THE 1.3 PER CENT WITHHOLDING RATE IS A DEFAULT-GRID RATE, which is the correct conservative choice for someone with no established tax history, i.e. precisely an early-career graduate, and is itself flagged above as my lookup rather than the page's own figure.
evidence_limitations: Not a graduate figure: the gross input is a French immigration salary floor, not a measured graduate wage, and it sits above the typical French graduate starting salary, so this net overstates what most new graduates take home. No official French statistics body publishes a national median monthly take-home for graduates; INSEE publishes gross wage distributions by decile, not take-home. Private-sector, non-cadre, under 65, resident in metropolitan France. Excludes employer contributions, which the employee never bears, so the employee's total burden is not 20.44 per cent of gross once employer contributions are counted. The net imposable calculation and the 1.3 per cent default withholding rate are the least firmly sourced parts and are separately flagged. A resident of Guadeloupe, La Réunion, Martinique, Guyane or Mayotte faces different official PAS grids, archived alongside.
